This scope never calls `pushUndo` itself (confirmed by grep restricted to 9642-9934 — zero hits). Undo coverage for the mutating chords in this scope is entirely delegated to the out-of-scope functions it dispatches to by name: `duplicateLayer`/`duplicateSelection`/`duplicateSelectedFrames` each call their own undo snapshot internally (e.g. `duplicateLayer` calls `pushUndoLayers(true)` itself, timeline.js:1271, out of scope); `SMMotion`'s keyframe-editing chords (Easy Ease, interpolation, delete, nudge) manage their own undo inside motion.js, out of scope. By contrast, Select-All's own `state.selectedStrokeIndices` write, and the B/N work-area writes to `state.waIn`/`state.waOut`, have NO undo snapshot associated with them anywhere in this scope's own body — consistent with them being selection/session state rather than document content.

It dispatches to `SMMotion`'s own property-reveal, keyframe-interpolation, and keyframe-selection machinery but performs no rendering or frame materialization itself — every visual update after one of these chords is left to the callee (`SMMotion.*`, out of scope) or to the ambient render loop.
